subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard read/exec deny boundary for that skill, or remain an eligibility/prompt-visibility flag with a separate strict security policy?
rationale: The current code and docs support the reporter's source-level concern, but changing the meaning of `enabled:false` is a security and compatibility decision that affects agent tools, sandboxing, Gateway/UI semantics, and operator expectations.

options.title: Promote enabled:false to hard deny
options.body: Treat disabled skills as unavailable to read and execute, document the stronger contract, and add focused compatibility/security tests across read and exec surfaces.

options.title: Add a separate strict boundary
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` as eligibility and add an explicit strict skill-access policy for deployments that need hard isolation.

options.title: Document trusted-skill-only scope
options.body: Close the request as outside the supported trust model and update docs/UI wording so operators do not mistake the toggle for a sandbox.

recommendation.title: Promote enabled:false to hard deny
recommendation.body: Treat disabled skills as unavailable to read and execute, document the stronger contract, and add focused compatibility/security tests across read and exec surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is primarily security/product semantics and documentation alignment, and this owner has recent security/docs history around the affected skill surface.
